_meta.note: The adapter is the Real Adapter Contract lane's pinned build (test/real_adapters/package.json, npm ci): codex-acp 2.2.2, driven over stdio by a scratch client against a loopback Responses-API model stub, so no real model or credential was involved. The stub finds the target tool in the request's own tool list and asks for it with one function_call, then answers with the function_call_output it got back. After session/new the client sets mode read-only over session/set_config_option, the routing Crew arms on every codex session (Routing.SESSION_CONFIG), and answers the permission request allow_once. Agent-to-client lines verbatim and in order, with these reductions at capture: the session uuid is a fixed name and the scratch working directory reads ~/work; the available_commands_update frame (the adapter's command inventory) is dropped; models.availableModels is emptied and each multi-option select in configOptions keeps only its current value, as codex/session-live.jsonl does. The session/new array carried exactly one element: members.member_dispatch_session_server('probe-member-key'), the kirocrew-dashboard stdio entry AcpRuntime appends for a member session, with its gateway port pointed where nothing listens so no call reached a live gateway. The model's call reached the mounted server: tool_call mcp.kirocrew-dashboard.session_status, a session/request_permission marked is_mcp_tool_approval, and a completed tool_call_update carrying the server's own answer, which refuses because it cannot reach the gateway for the probe key's tool policy. So the element is mounted and its tool reachable under the read-only routing.
